_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC BOS. Overlaid onto the schema built from BosConfig (a SosFadeConfig superset). UI ONLY — never touches a trade decision or the source hash. Click Scan Strategies after editing. THE CONTRACT: `label` is the Pine input's TITLE and `desc` is its TOOLTIP, both verbatim from indicators/strategies/mpc_bos_strategy.pine, changed in the same commit — one parameter, one name, one explanation, two UIs. They were EXTRACTED from the Pine by script rather than retyped, because a lab row saying something different from the chart is how a rule gets read backwards (exec_deep_fib said 'ABOVE' where its own tooltip said 'shallower', and that was false half the time). Params not listed here fall back to their raw field names; the inherited A+ fields that this fork pins are deliberately absent, because none of them is an input in this fork's Pine — see config.py for why each is pinned. COPY STYLE (2026-08-10, Aaron's call): every desc is SHORT and PLAIN — what the setting does, what each choice means, and the one fact that changes the decision. No measurement dumps, no trade counts, no R figures, no dates, no file references: the strategy detail page is for reading, and the evidence behind a default lives in this package's CLAUDE.md and its optimization doc. Same rule for `edge` and `steps`.
edge: A break of structure says the trend has turned. What comes after it is what this trades: the market keeps breaking in the same direction until it turns again, and each break gives a pullback to buy or sell into. The main bot fades the turn; this one rides what the turn started. Not every break is real, so it is filtered hard. Nothing here has been checked against the TradingView chart yet, so read the direction of a result and never the exact numbers.

steps.label: 01 · Turn
steps.title: A shift opens a run
steps.detail: Structure breaks and opens a run on that side. Until it does, nothing can trade.

steps.label: 02 · Break
steps.title: A continuation break sets up a trade
steps.detail: Each later break in the same direction is a fresh setup. The newest one always owns it — an older setup still waiting for its pullback is dropped.

steps.label: 03 · Pullback
steps.title: A limit rests in the pullback
steps.detail: An order rests at the chosen depth and fills the moment price touches it. The setup dies if price runs out of room or the time limit passes first.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Out at the last target or the stop
steps.detail: The first target moves the stop to breakeven and the second lifts it further. By default nothing is banked early: the whole position leaves at the last target, or at the stop that has been climbing behind it.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: Take long trades. Off = the long side never arms, and every long setup that was ready is logged as blocked, so you can still count what it cost.
params._desc_note: No tooltip on the Pine input — written here. Copy it back to the Pine before treating it as the shared text.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: Take short trades. Off = the short side never arms, and every short setup that was ready is logged as blocked.
params._desc_note: No tooltip on the Pine input — written here. Copy it back to the Pine before treating it as the shared text.

params.name: bos_which
params.label: Which break after the shift
params.desc: Which break after the turn to trade. The first break is the initial push; the rest are continuations. All is the default — taking every break tested better. Note a new break always cancels an older setup still waiting for its pullback.

params.name: bos_min_disp_atr
params.label: Break must clear the swing by (x ATR)
params.desc: How far the breaking candle must close past the level it broke, measured in ATR. A one-tick poke through a high is a stop run, not a break. 0 = accept any break.

params.name: bos_min_leg_atr
params.label: Break leg must be at least (x ATR)
params.desc: The smallest move that counts as a break. A tiny move leaves a pullback inside the noise, with a stop too tight to survive and targets inside the spread. 0 = no minimum.

params.name: bos_max_days
params.label: Drop an armed break after (days)
params.desc: How long a setup waits for its pullback before it is dropped. Counted in bars rather than clock time, so weekends and the daily close do not use it up.

params.name: bos_max_per_regime
params.label: Max trades between shifts
params.desc: Stop taking new trades after this many fills since the last turn, until the next one. 10 is effectively off. Lower it to 2 or 3 to stop losses stacking up in one choppy stretch.

params.name: bos_req_hold
params.label: Broken level must hold
params.desc: On = a candle closing back through the broken level kills the setup. Careful: with the entry this deep, price normally has to close back through that level to reach the order at all, so the setup usually dies just before it would have filled. It only makes sense with a much shallower entry.

params.name: bos_fib_anchor
params.label: Measure levels on
params.desc: Which move the entry, the stop and the targets are measured on. Break leg freezes them at the break. Expansion leg keeps measuring while price runs, so the levels move until the pullback starts. Break leg is the default because every tested number here was produced that way — the two have never been compared.

params.name: bos_entry_top
params.label: Shallowest the entry may rest
params.desc: The shallowest pullback the strategy will accept. Shallow entries fill far more often and pay far less, because the stop stays where it is while the targets come closer, so the whole ladder compresses. The deep end does not move. Not measured — this is a lever to test.

params.name: bos_use_fvg
params.label: Price the entry off a gap
params.desc: On = the order is placed on a gap inside the pullback. Off is the default = a plain level, and the five settings below grey out. Off, because pricing the entry off a gap was the losing half of the book: the gap decides where the order rests, and it rests too shallow.

params.name: exec_req_fvg
params.label: ↳ ...and require one (no gap = no trade)
params.desc: On = if no gap qualifies, the setup does not trade at all. Off = it still trades, at the plain level further down. The shallow pocket counts as a gap here, so a setup that has one is not refused.

params.name: exec_fvg_deep_only
params.label: ↳ ...gap must sit fully past the shallow end
params.desc: On = the whole gap has to sit on the deep side of the shallow end set above. Off = a gap lying across that line also counts. Deeper entries are better prices but are reached less often.

params.name: exec_deep_fib
params.label: ↳ ...deep gap enters at the nearest fib
params.desc: For a gap sitting deeper than 0.618: rest the order at the nearest level just above the gap — the price you reach first — instead of chasing the gap's own edge, which price may never touch.

params.name: exec_conf_sz2
params.label: ↳ ...Sniper Zone counts as a gap
params.desc: Lets the shallow pocket of the break stand in for a gap on a setup that had none. Off = a real gap is strictly required. It can price a trade; it is never something the trade waits for.

params.name: exec_fvg_50
params.label: ↳ ...gap across the shallow end enters at it
params.desc: Last resort: a gap lying across the shallow end of the band rests the order exactly on that line. Ranked below every other source, so it only ever prices a setup nothing better could.

params.name: bos_entry_fib
params.label: Fallback entry level
params.desc: How deep in the pullback the order rests. This is what actually trades, since pricing off a gap is off by default — the name is left over. Deeper tested clearly better. Do not pair a deep entry with a tighter stop: the stop ends up so small that the spread eats most of the trade.

params.name: bos_respect_veto
params.label: Divergence blocks a new entry
params.desc: On = a long will not open while a bearish divergence is live or momentum is extremely overbought, and the mirror for shorts. It is re-checked every bar, so a divergence appearing while the setup waits pulls the order, and the order can go back if it fades.

params.name: bos_vwap_req
params.label: Session VWAP filter
params.desc: Only trade while price is closing on the trend's own side of the session average price — above it for a long, below for a short. It asks which side price is on, not whether it crossed. It looked good in testing, but on a simplified version of this setup, so treat it as a hint.

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-18:00 NY)
params.desc: Blocks new entries in the last hour before the daily close. Gold closes at 17:00 New York and reopens at 18:00, so a trade opened late can be gapped out over the break. That is a fact about market hours rather than a strategy opinion.

params.name: exec_htf_weekly
params.label: Weekly bias requirement
params.desc: Whether the weekly trend has to agree with the trade. Ignore = no filter. Must agree = the weekly has to match. Must not oppose = neutral is fine, only an opposing weekly blocks. For a trend-following setup, Must agree is the natural one to try.

params.name: exec_htf_daily
params.label: Daily bias requirement
params.desc: The same four choices, judged on the daily trend. Ignore = off.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. Position size is worked out from this and the stop distance, so a wider stop automatically buys a smaller position.

params.name: bos_sl_model
params.label: Stop model
params.desc: Where the stop sits. ATR is a fixed distance from the entry and is the default: it was the biggest improvement measured here, because a level-based stop shrinks with the move and can end up inside the spread. Broken swing level sits the wrong side of the entry, so it refuses almost every order.

params.name: bos_sl_atr
params.label: ↳ ATR multiple
params.desc: How far the stop sits from the entry, in ATR, when the stop model above is ATR. Anything from about 1.2 to 1.5 gives the same answer, so read it as a range rather than an exact number. Below 1.0 the stop starts landing inside the spread again, which is the problem this stop model exists to remove.

params.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
params.label: Extra room beyond the stop (ticks)
params.desc: Pushes the stop this many ticks further away than the level chosen above, so a wick through it does not take you out.

params.name: exec_min_stop_mode
params.label: Minimum stop distance
params.desc: Refuse a setup whose stop lands too close to the entry. Size is risk divided by stop distance, so a stop that collapses onto the entry does not risk less — it buys an enormous position that ordinary noise runs straight through. With the ATR stop above it rarely fires, so treat it as a second line of defence.

params.name: exec_min_stop_val
params.label: ↳ Minimum stop floor (unit = mode above)
params.desc: The floor itself. A percent in percent-of-price mode, dollars of price in fixed mode, a multiple in ATR mode.

params.name: bos_move_stop
params.label: Moving stop (trails from entry)
params.desc: A trailing stop that starts as soon as you are filled, instead of waiting for the second target. It follows the best price the trade has seen and can only ever tighten. Off = the stop stays put until the first target moves it to breakeven.

params.name: bos_move_stop_val
params.label: ↳ trail distance (unit = mode above)
params.desc: How far the moving stop sits behind the best price seen. Dollars of price in dollar mode — on gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 5.0 is 50 pips — or ticks behind the last swing in structure mode. Too tight and normal noise scratches every trade before it can work, so start wide and walk it in.

params.name: exec_tp1_pct
params.label: TP1 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the first target banks. 0 is the default and banking here tested worse. Touching the target still moves the stop to breakeven whatever this is set to, so 0 keeps the protection and gives up only the partial.

params.name: exec_tp2_pct
params.label: TP2 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the second target banks. 0 by default, for the same reason. Touching it still lifts the stop to its floor and hands the rest onward, so the targets drive the stop whatever the sizes are.

params.name: exec_tp3_pct
params.label: TP3 size %
params.desc: How much of the position the last target banks. That target is the far end of the move. 100 is the default, so there is no runner: the whole position leaves there or at the stop climbing behind it, which tested best. Anything under 100 turns the rest into a runner again.

params.name: bos_tp3_measured
params.label: TP3 = measured move
params.desc: Replaces the last target with the classic continuation target: the size of the break projected forward from the level it broke. That sits further out than the end of the move. Ignored when it would land behind the second target. On a shallow entry it is what creates a last target at all.

params.name: exec_be_buf_tk
params.label: Breakeven buffer (ticks)
params.desc: The breakeven stop sits this far beyond the entry, so a scratch still covers costs instead of losing a few cents. It is also why TradingView reports no breakevens — those exits book a tiny profit, so it files them as wins. The trade label counts them honestly.

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the last part of the position is trailed once the second target is hit. Structure parks the stop at the last swing — it breathes with the trend and usually rides further, but a swing lags, so it hands some back at the turn. Fixed step ratchets on the grid set below.

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: ↳ Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: Structure method only. The trailing stop sits this many ticks beyond the swing it is following, so a wick through it does not clip the trade.

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: The step size in dollars. Read by two settings, so it is never greyed out: the fixed-step trail ratchets on this grid, and the one-step-behind floor sits this far under the best price seen. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit, before the trail takes over. TP1 price is tight and can scratch the trade on the first pullback. Breakeven gives it the most room. The trail can still tighten past this, never loosen it.

params.name: bos_close_opp_div
params.label: Close an open trade on opposing divergence
params.desc: On = close the trade when a divergence confirms against it, rather than waiting for the stop or a target — it says the move is overstretched and the next turn is building. It fires on a confirmed divergence only, never on a plain overbought reading.
